frase_gancho.texto: Winged dances amid the mountain mist that celebrate harmony with the earth.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Located at the head of the upper floor, this hall explores the dynamic microcosm of the Sierra Norte de Puebla, where the Nahua, Totonac, Otomi, and Tepehua live side by side. Despite their linguistic differences, these communities share a rugged territory and a deep devotion centered on the cultivation of corn and coffee. Visitors can admire the ritual beauty of traditional garments such as the quechquémitl, the making of ceremonial Amate Paper, and the symbolic spectacle of ancestral dances such as the Voladores (Flyers) and the Quetzales. The exhibition reveals how respect for the forces of nature sustains harmony.
